summary: Intermittent mixed-egress (eu -> us) correlated with non-deterministic DNS resolve order after region pin
description: Issue summary: Customer reports periodic high p95 latency and occasional US egress for requests pinned to eu-west. Impact: NimbleDocs production traffic sees 200-400ms p95 increases during mixed-egress windows, affecting synchronous user-facing endpoints. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated), prod, region eu-west. Problem started ~2026-03-08 10:00 UTC, intermittent since then.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create requests to Redwood inference API with customer API key (NimbleDocs dedicated pool) pinned to eu-west.
2) Issue sustained traffic at ~150rps for 30 minutes.
3) Observe p95 latency and trace egress path via X-Redwood-Egress header and traceroute.
4) Reproduceable window observed during control-plane pin refresh events and DNS TTL expiration windows.
observed_behavior: Approximately every 20-45 minutes a subset (~1.2-3%) of requests resolve to US egress nodes. X-Redwood-Egress headers show us-east carrier and traceroute shows a US hop. p95 increases by +220-340ms for affected requests. Customer sees mixed latencies and intermittent timeouts in synthetic monitors.
expected_behavior: All traffic pinned to eu-west should consistently egress via eu-west nodes. Any fallback to other regions should be deterministic based on residency policy and documented (strict vs best-effort), and should not be caused by non-deterministic DNS resolve order.
logs_snippets:
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] request_id=abc123 key=n-docs-pool egress_hint=eu-west resolved_ip=18.197.22.11
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] request_id=abc123 egress_selected=eu-west node=eu-serve-17 latency=98ms
[2026-03-10T14:34:21Z] request_id=def456 key=n-docs-pool egress_hint=eu-west resolved_ip=3.215.14.7
[2026-03-10T14:34:21Z] request_id=def456 egress_selected=us-east node=us-serve-05 latency=330ms
[DNS] eu-west-record A: 18.197.22.11, 3.215.14.7 TTL=60
[CONTROL-PLANE] pin-refresh initiated for pool n-docs-pool at 2026-03-10T14:30:00Z
investigation_notes: Initial triage: DNS answers include both eu and us candidate IPs (legacy multi-region A records) and client-side resolver behavior appears to select differing IP order across requests. Correlation found between control-plane pin refresh events and windows where DNS TTLs expire; resolver re-query returns same set but in different order. The serving runtime uses the first healthy IP from the resolution list to pick egress node, which causes non-deterministic selection when multiple region candidates are present. Checked firewall and routing tables on dedicated pool — no obvious BGP flapping. No related config changes from customer side.
root_cause_hypothesis: Control-plane pin refresh triggers A-record rotation with multi-region candidates for backward-compatibility. Because some resolvers do not preserve original order and our egress-selection picks the first returned IP, requests can be steered to non-local egress nodes. Combined with short DNS TTL (60s) this yields intermittent mixed-egress and p95 spikes.
mitigation_and_workaround: 1) Short-term: We can force stickiness on the serving side by preferring known-local CIDR ranges before honoring first-IP order. This reduces mixed-egress while we implement DNS ordering fixes. 2) Customer workaround: increase retry tolerance and add client-side resolver caching to avoid reordering windows (not ideal). 3) Control-plane: temporarily increase pin TTL to reduce frequency of A-record rotations.
next_steps:
- SRE to deploy a serving-side patch that filters resolution results by locality before choosing egress (PR created).
- DNS team to audit A-record generation to ensure region-first ordering for residency-bound pools.
- Schedule coordinated rollout with NimbleDocs; monitor p95 and X-Redwood-Egress headers during test window.
- Postmortem action: update runbook to include resolver behavior checklist for dedicated pools.
resolution: In progress: We merged a serving-side guard (PR https://github.com/redwood-infra/infra/pull/4821) that prefers eu CIDRs for eu-west pinned pools and rolled it to 10% of nodes at 2026-03-12T03:00Z UTC. Early metrics: mixed-egress rate dropped from ~1.5% to 0.15% in the canary pool and p95 improved by ~150ms for affected requests. Full rollout pending DNS ordering fix and customer verification.
